production.note: US model years 1998-2002 for the LS1 Trans Am. End: Edmunds 2002: 'Entering its last year of production, the Firebird gets few changes for 2002.' Start: Edmunds 1998: 'The new-for-1998 LS1 V8 is good for 305 horsepower' (edmunds-firebird-1998-review). The 1993-1997 LT1 Trans Am of the same generation is a different car.

body.note: 'convertible versions of the Firebird and the Trans Am (but not the Formula) are available'

configuration.note: Cars.com '2dr Cpe Trans Am'; LS1 V8.

displacementL.note: 'Displacement: 5.7L/346'. The Auto Channel (Carey Russ, 1999): '5.7 liters / 347 cu. in.' (autochannel-trans-am-1999). No opened page prints the cc figure.

aspiration.note: Inferred: Corvette-derived LS1, no forced induction.

transmission.note: 'All V8 models come standard with a four-speed automatic transmission; a six-speed manual is a no-cost option.' Cars.com 1998: '6-Speed M/T ... 4-Speed A/T' (cars-com-trans-am-1998).

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (databases and articles). 1998 Trans Am, standard (non-Ram Air) engine. Quote (KBB 1998 Trans Am Coupe 2D): "305 @ 5200 RPM". Cars.com 1998 '2dr Cpe Trans Am': "SAE Net Horsepower: 305 @ 5200" (cars-com-trans-am-1998). The Auto Channel (John Heilig, 1998 Trans Am convertible): "HORSEPOWER/TORQUE: 305 hp @ 5,200 rpm/335 lb-ft @ 4,000 rpm" (autochannel-trans-am-1998). Edmunds: "The new-for-1998 LS1 V8 is good for 305 horsepower" (edmunds-firebird-1998-review). 2002: KBB "310 @ 5200 RPM" (kbb-firebird-2002); Edmunds 2002 'standard 310 horsepower'. The Ram Air WS6 Performance and Handling Package added 15 hp (Edmunds 1998; 320 hp, Carey Russ 1999 30th Anniversary: "320 @ 5200 rpm"; 325 hp in 2002) and is a package, not a separate trim. Reference year 1998: 305 hp is taken to cover 1998-2000 and 310 hp 2001-2002, but no page opened confirms the 2000 and 2001 Trans Am ratings individually.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (databases). 1998 Trans Am coupe; KBB names the automatic, the standard transmission; no source gives a manual-car figure. Quote (KBB 1998 Trans Am Coupe 2D page): "Curb Weight | 3479 lbs." (KBB's general 1998 Firebird page shows 3,453 lb, which is the Formula). Cars.com 1998 '2dr Cpe Trans Am': "Base Curb Weight: 3,488 lbs" (cars-com-trans-am-1998), 0.3% higher; see discrepancies. Heilig's 1998 convertible: "CURB WEIGHT: 3,605 lbs"; KBB 2002 Trans Am Coupe 2D: "3,499 pounds" (kbb-firebird-2002).

discrepancies.reason: Cars.com gives 3,488 lb for the 1998 Trans Am coupe, KBB 3,479 lb (automatic, the standard transmission); 0.3% apart.
discrepancies.resolution: KBB's 3,479 lb used for the standard (automatic) coupe; the difference is well within 2%.

provisionalNote: Power (305 hp) rests on databases (KBB, Cars.com) and articles (The Auto Channel, Edmunds), all agreeing. Weight (3,479 lb) rests on KBB's Trans Am page, with Cars.com 3,488 lb (0.3% higher). A Pontiac/GM 1998 press kit, spec sheet or brochure, or a major magazine spec panel for the 1998 Trans Am, would replace both.
